subject.title: [Bug]: Windows gateway listens but local health/status time out after Telegram polling stall (v2026.5.20)

question: Should repeated unrecovered Telegram/channel stalls escalate to supervised Gateway process recovery, or should OpenClaw keep recovery inside channel/session layers until an affected-host repro identifies the exact blocker?
rationale: Current code intentionally caps channel restart attempts without exiting, while the reported failure is process-level unresponsiveness; changing that boundary affects operator recovery behavior and active sessions.

options.title: Reproduce First, Then Choose Recovery
options.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical thread, collect current-main affected-host proof, and decide process-level recovery only if channel/session fixes still leave Gateway probes timing out.

options.title: Add Supervised Recovery Policy
options.body: Define and implement a bounded Gateway watchdog or process-exit policy for unrecovered channel stalls with upgrade notes and Windows proof.

options.title: Stay Channel-Scoped
options.body: Continue closing only narrower Telegram transport/session bugs and do not add process-level recovery unless a fresh repro proves it is necessary.

recommendation.title: Reproduce First, Then Choose Recovery
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical thread, collect current-main affected-host proof, and decide process-level recovery only if channel/session fixes still leave Gateway probes timing out.

likelyOwner.reason: They already ran the targeted repro attempt and have recent merged history in the Telegram polling watchdog area most relevant to the remaining policy and proof gap.
